mechanism: Higher funded defense budgets and stockpile replenishment can become missile, air-defense, naval, sensor, and engine awards that RTX converts through qualified production, deliveries, and sustainment into revenue, segment profit, cash flow, and backlog; shareholder transmission depends on pricing, productivity, mix, fixed-price execution, suppliers, export approvals, commercial aerospace, Pratt remediation, leverage, and valuation.
catalyst: Funded missile, air-defense, naval, sensor, and engine awards lift qualified output; defense backlog converts into deliveries; Raytheon margins and group free cash flow improve; Pratt remediation costs decline; and inventory, receivables, contract assets, and fixed-price provisions remain controlled while capacity expands.
invalidation: Defense budgets fail to become funded awards; replenishment urgency fades; export approvals or supplier constraints prevent delivery; production expansion creates quality failures; fixed-price charges absorb volume; commercial aerospace declines; Pratt remediation liabilities rise; leverage constrains capital allocation; or defense growth fails to produce sustained group-level free cash flow.
